hash-2.upside: Figure has promised a fee model that would make HASH pay for network use, and Provenance's locked value grew strongly this year; no launch date is set.
hash-2.cheap: It isn't cheap at about $450M with only about $116K traded a day; few people can trade it, which is why it's ignored.
hash-2.wrongIf: No fee-model launch date announced by end of Q1 2027, or daily trading stays under $100K.
hash-2.vsScanner: The 34x trading spike comes from a tiny base on one exchange (Figure Markets); not a catalyst.

elsa.upside: A working AI trading-assistant app with many exchange listings; the only dated event is a token unlock, which is a headwind, not upside.
elsa.cheap: Down about 85% from its January high because only 29% of tokens are out and more keep unlocking every week.
elsa.wrongIf: Price falls below about $0.05 after the unlock around Nov 19-20, or the app goes quiet into December.
elsa.vsScanner: The scanner's 'healthy trading' hides that this is mostly unlock-driven selling and speculative spikes (+46% on Nov 5 with no news).

nodecoin.upside: Nodepay claims over 2 million users of its bandwidth-sharing app; nothing dated is coming.
nodecoin.cheap: It fell about 99.8% from its 2025 launch as airdrop farmers sold; the market sees it as a farmed-out airdrop token.
nodecoin.wrongIf: Daily trading drops under $50K or no product news by end of December.
nodecoin.vsScanner: The scanner can't see its life status; I couldn't find any news newer than a May 2026 partnership, so it's weaker than the score suggests.

netx.upside: A small payments/RWA chain with an AI angle; I found no dated upgrade or listing coming.
netx.cheap: Little known and only on Gate and MEXC; no clear reason the market is missing it.
netx.wrongIf: No dated upgrade or new exchange listing announced by end of December, or the price falls another 30% to under $0.085.
netx.vsScanner: Agree the trading is decent, but I could not confirm the team or any real usage.

alexgo.upside: The DAO ended token emissions in late October and moved to buybacks and burns, which removes steady selling; effect should show over the next 1-3 months.
alexgo.cheap: It was hacked (about $8M stolen) and lost trust; few are watching a small Stacks DeFi app.
alexgo.wrongIf: Buybacks don't show up on-chain by end of January, or trading volume on its DEX keeps shrinking.
alexgo.vsScanner: The scanner calls it a zombie because its GitHub is old; the October governance change shows the project is still being run, so I'd call it quiet rather than dead.

numinous.upside: A working AI forecasting subnet that could win a bigger share of Bittensor rewards; no dated event.
numinous.cheap: Subnet tokens are thin and ignored after Bittensor's governance changes.
numinous.wrongIf: Its share of subnet rewards falls or daily trading stays under $30K.
numinous.vsScanner: The 3x trading jump with price only up 2% is noise.

clearpool.upside: Moving its lending business to the XRP Ledger with a new CLEAR token; the swap window opened 2026-11-17 and runs to 2027-02-17.
clearpool.cheap: Migrations confuse holders and data sites; trackers dropped CPOOL, so it's temporarily invisible.
clearpool.wrongIf: CLEAR doesn't get exchange support (price data on CoinGecko) by mid-December, or XRPL lending volume doesn't appear by end of Q1 2027.
clearpool.vsScanner: The scanner shows it as gone; it was migrated 1:1 to CLEAR, not delisted. Supply rises 12.5% in the swap.

topPicksNote: Nothing on today's short list has a dated, verified catalyst; the only real projects (Provenance, HeyElsa, ALEX) either have no date or face unlock selling.
